entry: American aerospace and defense corporation. Founded in 1916 by William E. Boeing in [[Seattle]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], it designs and manufactures [[Airplane|airplanes]], rotorcraft, [[Rocket|rockets]], [[Satellite|satellites]], and [[Missile|missiles]], and it also provides leasing and product support. The present corporation resulted from its acquisition of McDonnell Douglas on August 1, 1997. Boeing is organized into three primary divisions. In 2021 it recorded $62.3 billion in sales, and its headquarters are in Arlington County, Virginia, near Washington, DC.

Early American long-range narrow-body airliner. It was the first jetliner developed and produced by Boeing Commercial Airplanes. Developed from the Boeing 367-80 prototype, the initial 707-120 first flew on December 20, 1957, and [[Pan Am]] began regular service with the type on October 26, 1958. Although it was not the first commercial jetliner in service, it was the first to be widespread and is often credited with beginning the Jet Age. It dominated passenger air transport in the 1960s. In total, 856 Boeing 707s and 154 Boeing 720s were produced and delivered.

American narrow-body airliner. Developed to supplement the Boeing 727 on short and thin routes, it kept the width of the [[Boeing 707]] fuselage and its six-abreast seating. The 737-100 first flew in April 1967 and entered service with [[Lufthansa]] in February 1968. It was the best-selling commercial aircraft until the [[Airbus A320 family]] surpassed it in October 2019. The 737 MAX was grounded worldwide from March 2019 to November 2020 after two fatal crashes. As of October 2026, 17,791 had been ordered and 12,772 delivered.

American wide-body four-engined long-range airliner. Designed and manufactured by Boeing Commercial Airplanes, it first flew on February 9, 1969, and entered service with [[Pan Am]] on January 22, 1970. It was the first airplane called a "Jumbo Jet". Boeing built 1,574 aircraft over a 54-year production run that ended with a freighter delivered to Atlas Air in January 2023. Freighter variants remain popular with cargo airlines, and larger variants of the [[Boeing 777]] ultimately superseded later 747s.

American long-range wide-body airliner, often called the Triple Seven. It is the world's largest twinjet and the most-built wide-body airliner. Launched in October 1990 with an order from [[United Airlines]], it entered service with that launch operator in June 1995. It was the first Boeing airliner to use fly-by-wire controls. As of October 2026, 1,798 had been delivered, making it the best-selling wide-body airliner.

American twin-turboshaft attack [[Helicopter|helicopter]] with a tandem cockpit for a crew of two. Developed by Hughes Helicopters as the Model 77 for the U.S. Army's Advanced Attack Helicopter program, its prototype first flew on September 30, 1975. The Apache entered U.S. Army service in April 1986. It is armed with a 30 mm M230 chain gun and typically carries AGM-114 Hellfire missiles. As of March 2024, over 2,700 had been delivered to the U.S. Army and 18 international partners and allies. It is the primary attack helicopter of several nations, including [[Greece]], [[Japan]], [[Israel]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Singapore]], and the [[United Arab Emirates]].

American four-engined propeller-driven heavy [[Bomber|bomber]] designed by [[Boeing]]. It was flown mainly during [[World War II]] and the [[Korean War]]. Silverplate B-29s dropped the atomic bombs on [[Hiroshima]] and [[Nagasaki]], and they remain the only system to deliver [[Nuclear weapon|nuclear weapons]] in combat. Its $3 billion cost of design and production made it the most expensive program of the war, far exceeding the $1.9 billion cost of the [[Manhattan Project]]. Of 3,970 built, 22 have survived in preservation, and two still fly.

American nuclear-capable subsonic jet-powered strategic [[Bomber|bomber]] designed and built by [[Boeing]]. Built to carry nuclear weapons for [[Cold War]] deterrence, it replaced the Convair B-36 Peacemaker and has been operated by the United States Air Force since 1955. It can carry up to 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of weapons, with a typical combat range of around 8,800 miles without aerial refueling. The B-52 has used conventional munitions in the [[Vietnam War]], the [[Gulf War]], and the [[Iraq War]]. The B-52H is the only operational variant, scheduled to be upgraded as the B-52J by 2030.

[[Wetland]] type with [[Peat|peat]]-rich soil, one of the four main kinds of wetland. Other names include mire, quagmire, and muskeg, and alkaline mires are called fens. Bogs occur where surface water is [[Acid|acidic]] and low in nutrients, and most of their water comes from precipitation rather than mineral-rich groundwater. Low oxygen levels slow decay, so dead material, often [[Sphagnum|sphagnum]] moss, accumulates as peat, and large areas can be covered many meters deep in it. Bogs are widely distributed in cold, temperate climes, mostly in boreal ecosystems of the [[Northern Hemisphere]]. The world's largest wetland is the peat bogs of the Western Siberian Lowlands in [[Russia]], which cover more than a million sq km. Bogs support distinctive species and are of high importance for [[Biodiversity|biodiversity]].

Mythical creature used to frighten children into good behavior. Bogeymen take many forms across cultures, but they are most commonly depicted as [[Monster|monsters]] that punish children for misbehaving, and authority figures often invoke them to discourage specific acts. The term is sometimes used as a metonym for terror and sometimes for the [[Devil]]. It may derive from the [[Middle English]] *bugge* or *bogge*, meaning "frightening specter". The word is known from the 15th century, though bogeyman stories are likely much older.

Capital and largest city of [[Colombia]]. Founded on August 6, 1538, by Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada as the capital of the New Kingdom of Granada, it was renamed Bogotá by [[Simón Bolívar]] to honor the Muisca people. After the Battle of Boyacá on August 7, 1819, it became the capital of [[Gran Colombia]]. The city lies on a high [[Plateau|plateau]] in the [[Andes]] at an average altitude of 2,640 m, the third highest capital city in the world. It is the country's main financial and business center, generating almost a quarter (24.7%) of national GDP. Its El Dorado International Airport handles the largest cargo volume in Latin America.

Ruthenian nobleman and military commander, hetman of the Zaporozhian Host from 1648 to 1657. He led the [[Cossacks]] to victory in an uprising against the [[Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth]] (1648–1654) that created an independent Cossack state in Dnieper Ukraine. Under his leadership, Cossacks massacred tens of thousands of Poles and Jews in 1648–1649, and the massacres continued until at least 1652, possibly causing hundreds of thousands of deaths. In 1654 he concluded the Treaty of Pereiaslav with the Russian tsar, allying the [[Cossack Hetmanate]] with [[Tsardom of Russia]] and placing Ukraine under Russian protection. Ukrainians have honored him as a folk hero and founder of the first Ukrainian state, while Russian imperial and Soviet propaganda promoted him as a "unifier" of Ukraine with Russia. In [[Western Europe]], he was compared with his rebel contemporary [[Oliver Cromwell]], and his image remained controversial because of his alliances and harsh policies.

Westernmost and largest historical region of the [[Czech Republic]]. In the 9th century it was a principality that became part of [[Great Moravia]], then an independent duchy and a kingdom within the [[Holy Roman Empire]]. It later belonged to the [[Habsburg monarchy]] and the Austrian Empire, and after World War I it became part of [[Czechoslovakia]]. Bohemia covers 52,065 sq km, and about 6.9 million of the Czech Republic's 10.9 million inhabitants live there.

1975 single by the British rock band [[Queen (band)|Queen]]. Written by [[Freddie Mercury]], it is the penultimate song on the album *A Night at the Opera* and a suite of five main elements: an introduction, a [[Ballad|ballad]], an [[Opera|opera]], a hard rock segment, and a reflective coda. Released as the lead single, it topped the UK Singles Chart for nine weeks, plus five more weeks after Mercury's death, and it is now regarded as the band's signature song. In the United States it peaked at number nine in 1976 before reaching number two in 1992 after appearing in the film *Wayne's World*. Its promotional video is credited with advancing the [[Music video|music video]] medium. The song ranked number 17 on [[Rolling Stone|*Rolling Stone*]]'s 2021 list of the "500 Greatest Songs of All Time", and in 2022 it was inducted into the National Recording Registry by the [[Library of Congress]].

Social and cultural movement centered on a way of life outside conventional norms. The term, from the French *bohème*, described mid-19th-century nonconformist lifestyles of artists, writers, journalists, musicians, and actors in major European cities. The French called [[Romani people|Romani]] *bohémiens*, because they were believed to have come from [[Bohemia]]. Henri Murger's 1845 stories *Scenes of Bohemian Life* formed the basis of [[Giacomo Puccini]]'s 1896 opera *La bohème*. Bohemians expressed unorthodox views through free love, frugality, and in some cases voluntary poverty. The term is not connected to the Czechs of historical Bohemia.

Obsolete atomic model incorporating early quantum concepts, developed by [[Niels Bohr]] from 1911 to 1918. Building on [[Ernest Rutherford]]'s discovery of the [[Atomic nucleus|atomic nucleus]], it places a small, dense nucleus surrounded by orbiting [[Electron|electrons]], an arrangement analogous to the [[Solar System]] but held together by electrostatic attraction rather than gravity. Electron energies are quantized, and the model explained the Rydberg formula for hydrogen's spectral lines. It replaced the plum pudding model of [[J. J. Thomson]], and the quantum atomic model superseded it in the 1920s. Because of its simplicity and correct results for selected systems, it is still taught to introduce students to quantum mechanics and energy level diagrams.

Family of nonvenomous [[Snake|snakes]], commonly known as boas or boids. Found mainly in the Americas, with some species in Africa, Europe, Asia, and Pacific islands, the family includes some of the world's largest snakes. The [[Anaconda|green anaconda]] of South America is the heaviest and second-longest snake known. The family comprises six subfamilies, 14–15 genera, and 54–67 [[Species|species]]. Boas kill prey by constriction, but death results from [[Asphyxia|suffocation]] rather than crushing, and prey is swallowed whole. Unlike pythons, boids lack postfrontal bones and premaxillary teeth, and they give birth to live young.

Rapid phase transition from [[Liquid|liquid]] to [[Gas|gas]], the reverse of [[Condensation|condensation]]. Boiling occurs when a liquid is heated to its [[Boiling point|boiling point]], where its vapor pressure equals the pressure of the surrounding atmosphere. Boiling and [[Evaporation|evaporation]] are the two main forms of vaporization. In nucleate boiling, bubbles form at discrete points on the heated surface, while in critical heat flux boiling a film of vapor forms on the surface, sharply reducing heat transfer. Water boils at 100 °C (212 °F) at sea level but at lower temperatures at high altitudes. Holding water at 100 °C for one minute inactivates most microorganisms and [[Virus|viruses]], and boiling is also used in cooking methods such as blanching, [[Steaming|steaming]], and poaching.

Characteristic temperature of a substance, at which the vapor pressure of its [[Liquid|liquid]] equals the surrounding pressure. Lower pressure lowers the boiling point, so water boils at 100 °C at [[Sea level|sea level]] under standard pressure but at 93.4 °C at 1,905 m altitude. The normal boiling point is the temperature at which vapor pressure equals one atmosphere, and IUPAC has defined the standard boiling point since 1982 as boiling under a pressure of one [[Bar (unit)|bar]]. Unlike evaporation, which occurs at the surface below the boiling point, boiling forms vapor bubbles throughout the liquid.

Capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of [[Idaho]] (pop., 2020: 235,685). Located on the Boise River in southwestern Idaho, it is the county seat of Ada County at an elevation of 2,704 ft (824 m) above [[Sea level|sea level]]. The metropolitan area in the Treasure Valley has an estimated 846,000 residents. Major employers in technology and manufacturing include Micron Technology and [[Hewlett-Packard]]. The city is home to the Idaho State Capitol, the annual Treefort Music Fest, and the Basque Block.

Leaf vegetable, a type of Chinese cabbage (*Brassica rapa* subsp. *chinensis*). Its varieties do not form heads; they have green leaf blades and lighter bulbous bottoms, and the flavor lies between that of [[Spinach|spinach]] and water chestnuts, slightly sweeter, with a mildly peppery undertone. Popular in southern China, [[East Asia|East Asia]], and [[Southeast Asia]], it belongs to the family [[Brassicaceae]]. Originally classified as *Brassica chinensis* by [[Carl Linnaeus]], it is now considered a subspecies of *Brassica rapa*. The name derives from [[Cantonese]] *baak choi*, meaning "white vegetable".

Jihadist militant organization based in northeastern [[Nigeria]], also active in [[Chad]], [[Niger]], Cameroon, and Mali. Founded by Mohammed Yusuf in 2002, its initial goal was to "purify" Sunni Islam in northern Nigeria. Since its insurgency began in 2009, it has killed tens of thousands of people and displaced 2.3 million, and the conflict has contributed to regional food crises and famines. In April 2014 it kidnapped 276 schoolgirls in Chibok, Borno State. In March 2015 the group pledged allegiance to the [[Islamic State|Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant]]. Its longtime leader Abubakar Shekau was confirmed dead in May 2021, and the group revived under Bakura Doro.

Duke of [[Poland]] (r. 992–1025) and the first King of Poland in 1025. Son of [[Mieszko I]] and a Bohemian princess, he reunified the country by 995 after banishing his father's widow and half-brothers. As a devout Christian he supported missionaries, and after Adalbert of Prague was martyred in 997 he ransomed the bishop's remains for their weight in gold, consolidating Poland's autonomy from the [[Holy Roman Empire]]. At the Congress of Gniezno in 1000, Emperor Otto III permitted a Polish church structure, and bishoprics were established at [[Kraków]], [[Wrocław]], and Kołobrzeg. He conquered territories including [[Slovakia]], Moravia, Lusatia, and [[Bohemia]], and he introduced the first Polish monetary unit, the grzywna.

Basidiomycete fungus, the type species of the [[Genus|genus]] *Boletus*, prized as an edible mushroom. Known as cep, penny bun, or porcino, it has a large brown cap that can reach 30 cm in diameter, with spore-releasing tubes beneath instead of gills. It forms symbiotic associations with trees, including [[Conifer|conifers]] and some hardwoods, and is widely distributed in the [[Northern Hemisphere]]. It is low in fat and digestible [[Carbohydrate|carbohydrates]] but high in [[Protein (nutrient)|protein]], vitamins, and minerals. Although sold commercially, it is very difficult to cultivate and is most often sold dried. French botanist Pierre Bulliard first described it in 1782.

Landlocked country in central [[South America]], officially the Plurinational State of Bolivia (pop., 2024: 11.4 million). Its west is Andean, including the high [[Altiplano]] plateau, with tropical lowlands to the east and north. The seat of government is [[La Paz]], the constitutional capital is Sucre, and the largest city is [[Santa Cruz de la Sierra]]. Before Spanish colonization the region formed part of the [[Tiwanaku]] polity. After an unsuccessful rebellion in Sucre on May 25, 1809, 16 years of fighting preceded the establishment of the republic, named for [[Simón Bolívar]]. The 1952 Bolivian National Revolution established universal suffrage and nationalized tin mining. Bolivia remains a developing country, the second-poorest in South America, though it has sharply reduced poverty rates. It is known for its production of [[Coca|coca]] and refined cocaine; in 2021, estimated coca cultivation and cocaine production were 39,700 hectares and 317 metric tons, respectively.
